text:
incbot: 🔔 Alert: Dedicated cluster 'eu-west-2-pool-3' p99 latency breach detected for streaming endpoints (p99 > 6s). Auto-escalation: paging oncall.
mae_oncall: ack - I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking runbook.
riggs_sre: pinging autoscaler metrics now. any initial customer impact reports?
sam_support: Support FYI — two customers reported 'streaming stalls' and one reported timeouts on long generations. Ticket IDs #4221 #4223.
devin_platform: pulling autoscaler and pool telemetry: `curl -s http://telemetry/api/pools/eu-west-2-pool-3/metrics | jq .` -> showing handshake_warmup_ms spike to 12_400ms over last 10m, queue_depth peaked at 2,300, and pending_requests ~480.
alyssa_prodeng: that handshake number is huge — warmup usually <300ms. Any recent kernel/quant changes?
mae_oncall: looking at deploy bot: `deploy-bot: rollout model variant v2-quant-lite to pool-3 completed 12m ago` — could be related.
riggs_sre: checking autoscaler logs: `autoscaler: warmup_retry timeout after 10s for slot init` repeated 1.2k times. It looks like the warmup handshake to the model runtime is timing out and causing slots to not come into ready state, so backlog builds.
mae_oncall: consequence: autoscaler doesn't bind new slots quickly, queue allows requests to pile, streaming sessions end up stuck waiting for first token -> stalls. p95 also creeping up to 1.1s but p99 is the real pain.
sam_support: customers flagged severity-high; Affected endpoints: streaming-chat, streaming-generate.
devin_platform: manual mitigation plan from runbook v3: (1) temporarily scale up pool capacity manually; (2) route traffic for top-tier customers to fallback pool; (3) reduce max_concurrency on pool to lower handshake pressure; (4) roll back v2-quant-lite if confirmed root cause.
mae_oncall: I'm executing manual scale now: `platformctl pools scale eu-west-2-pool-3 --count 18 --force` — starting to spin up 6 extra slots. watching handshake logs.
ops_bot: 6 new slots requested, warmup started.
riggs_sre: while they spin, we can enable 'fast-warmup' flag for the runtime to skip heavy quant stat pass: `runtimectl set-flag fast_warmup=true --pool eu-west-2-pool-3` — this reduces warmup by ~80% in testing. Recommend toggle while investigating.
alevent: mae_oncall: toggled fast_warmup=true. Observing handshake latency dropping to ~350ms for new slots.
mae_oncall: queue depth falling from 2300 -> 700 in last 90s. p99 down to ~3.2s but still above SLO.
alyssa_prodeng: good improvement. We should also consider routing internal canary for non-critical customers to fallback hosted models: `routingctl add-route --selector tier!=enterprise --target hosted-eu-2` for immediate relief.
sam_support: starting targeted routing for tickets #4221 #4223 to hosted fallback. customers notified: "Temporary reroute to hosted models while we mitigate; no model data persisted."
riggs_sre: digging into why quant-lite warmup spikes: core dump snippet from runtime: ```
[2026-03-15T15:02:11Z] warmup: quant_table_init took 12.1s
[2026-03-15T15:02:11Z] kernel-select: fallback to generic kernel due to memalign fail
``` Looks like a memory alignment/pathological kernel selection pattern causing quant table init to blow up only on certain GPU instances.
devin_platform: checking instance type distribution — a small subset (4/18) of the pool were provisioned on older driver version 525.x. Coordinator tried to place new slots there. We'll cordon those nodes.
mae_oncall: cordoning nodes now: `platformctl nodes cordon node-54 node-57 node-61` -> new slots avoided.
ops_bot: nodes cordoned. scheduler will avoid them for new allocations.
mae_oncall: after cordon + fast_warmup + manual scale, p95 ~0.6s, p99 ~1.4s and streaming stalls count reduced to single digits. Acceptable for immediate live mitigation.
alyssa_prodeng: next steps: (A) roll back v2-quant-lite to previous stable variant on eu-west-2-pool-3; (B) open issue to fleet provisioning to prevent older driver nodes from being assigned quant workloads; (C) add early warmup health probe so autoscaler can detect slow warmup and prefer fast_warmup mode.
riggs_sre: I'll take (B) and (C). Adding a metric alert for `warmup_latency > 2s for 2m` to trigger earlier paging.
mae_oncall: (A) rolling back: `deploy-bot rollback model v2-quant-lite --pool eu-west-2-pool-3 --to v1-stable` -> initiating.
devin_platform: rollback started. No config drift expected.
sam_support: updating affected customers: "We've applied temporary mitigations (reroute + scaling). We'll follow up with root cause and timeline for full remediation."
mae_oncall: verifying post-rollback metrics — warmup_latency normalizing, p99 ~0.45s now.
ops_bot: Incident note: manual scale + fast_warmup toggle + node cordon + rollback applied.
mae_oncall: closing on-call handoff: handing incident to eng-runtime for RCA and follow-up. cc @alyssa_prodeng @riggs_sre.
riggs_sre: will open an incident postmortem and tag impacted customers. Initial RCA hypothesis: v2-quant-lite introduced a quant init path that is sensitive to driver version; autoscaler coupled with heterogeneous node pool allowed slow warmup to starve capacity and cause backlog-driven streaming stalls.
alyssa_prodeng: assigning follow-ups: 1) fleet-provisioning blacklist for legacy driver nodes (owner: riggs_sre), 2) runtime warmup health probe + flagging (owner: devin_platform), 3) test matrix covering quant variants vs driver versions (owner: alyssa_prodeng).
mae_oncall: final status: mitigated, impact limited to a subset of streaming customers, tickets created for follow-up, monitoring alerts tuned. Leaving notes in incident channel.
incbot: 🔒 Incident resolved (mitigated) - create postmortem within 48h.
mae_oncall: copy. adding link to initial incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/3812345678 (RCA draft will be posted there).
riggs_sre: thanks all. going to draft timelines and add logs. anyone else with outstanding action items?
alyssa_prodeng: I'll own the test matrix.
sam_support: will follow up with customers and close the support tickets once RCA posted.
